# Declared inventory of the hosted app's Fly secrets — the managing-source of truth.
#
# Contract (enforced by .github/scripts/check-fly-secret-drift.py, issue #4126):
#   every name returned by `flyctl secrets list -a tortoise-y4mjjq` MUST appear
#   here, and its source MUST describe what keeps it in sync. A name that exists
#   only on Fly is drift by construction: it survives every deploy unversioned,
#   nobody can rotate it from GitHub, and CI cannot see it.
#
# Issue #4126 paid for this: `TORTOISE_SESSION_LLM_MODEL` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
# were hand-set on the Fly app with no managing source, the deployed key 403'd on
# every extraction call, and production answered 200 with `status: "partial"` /
# `extracted: 0` for 50/50 sessions — a total extraction outage no gate could see.
#
# FORMAT — `<NAME> <source>`, one per line. `#` comments and blank lines ignored.
#
# ⛔ A `gh-secret:<GH_NAME>` LINE MUST HAVE A MATCHING PROBE LINE in
#    deploy-hosted.yml's `GH_SECRETS_PRESENT` block. No CI token can list
#    repository secrets, so the deploy states which ones it carries; that is what
#    lets the gate fail on a declaration whose GitHub secret does not exist (the
#    #4126 incident: the guarded propagation was a permanent no-op and Fly kept a
#    hand-managed value). A name the probe omits reads as ABSENT, so a forgotten
#    line FAILS the deploy for that name rather than passing it — fail-closed, and
#    it names the exact variable to fix.
#
#   gh-secret:<GH_NAME>  propagated by .github/workflows/deploy-hosted.yml from
#                        the GitHub Actions secret <GH_NAME> (not always the same
#                        name — e.g. GITHUB_CLIENT_ID ← GH_CLIENT_ID). Verified
#                        both ways: a declaration the workflow no longer
#                        references is a violation, so this file cannot rot.
#   workflow             set by the workflow from non-secret context
#                        (${GITHUB_SHA}, a composed feature flag).
#   fly-toml-env         applied from fly.toml `[env]` — versioned, and the
#                        deploy applies it, so no Fly secret needs to exist.
#                        THREE states FAIL this declaration: the name is not an
#                        assigned key in fly.toml's `[env]` table; the deploy
#                        ASSIGNS the name (creating the secret that would shadow
#                        the versioned value); and a Fly secret of that name still
#                        EXISTS (the versioned value is not what the app reads).
#                        The last two are the same shadow, and the third is a
#                        TRANSITION rather than drift — the route (b) block below
#                        is the order that completes it, and it says which deploy
#                        may run while the state holds.
#   unmanaged            present on Fly with NO managing source. **This FAILS
#                        the gate** — it is the #4126 defect, not benign debt.
#                        The token names the state precisely so the failure is
#                        actionable: declare the real source
#                        (gh-secret:<GH_NAME> | workflow | fly-toml-env), or
#                        record the value in version control and drop the Fly
#                        secret. A gate that passes on a Fly-only variable is
#                        the fail-open #4126 was filed to close.
#   fly-only:<issue-ref> a DELIBERATELY out-of-band secret: it is managed
#                        outside BOTH GitHub and fly.toml on purpose, and the
#                        named issue carries the recorded decision (its
#                        `OVERRIDES:` marker states what the ruling overrides
#                        and why). `unmanaged` means "nobody declared a source";
#                        this token means "a source was deliberately refused,
#                        and here is the ruling". NOT a synonym for
#                        `unmanaged`: a bare `unmanaged` entry still FAILS the
#                        gate.
#                        The ref must be a WELL-FORMED, non-zero issue number —
#                        `<#N>` for this repo, or `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` for one
#                        elsewhere. `#0`, a non-ASCII digit (`\d` matches
#                        Arabic-Indic numerals), `#`, `#abc`, `#661abc`, `661`
#                        and a bare `owner/repo` are ALL a manifest the checker
#                        cannot read: exit 2, fail-closed, never a pass. The
#                        exception is only meaningful because of the issue it
#                        names, so an entry that names none is `unmanaged` in
#                        disguise.
#                        ⚠️ SHAPE ONLY: the checker is hermetic and offline, so
#                        it verifies the ref is a well-formed issue number — NOT
#                        that the issue exists or carries the ruling. A
#                        well-formed ref to a nonexistent issue passes; the
#                        existence half is a reviewer's job, and the `OVERRIDES:`
#                        marker on the named issue is what makes it checkable.
#                        Also FAILS a declaration whose name is not on Fly
#                        (there is nothing out-of-band to except), whose name
#                        the deploy assigns, or whose name is an assigned key in
#                        `fly.toml [env]` (version-controlled there, and a Fly
#                        secret would shadow that value — the same state the
#                        `fly-toml-env` route rejects).
#                        RESERVED for a decision that says the ABSENCE of a
#                        version-control source IS the property. THREE members are
#                        declared below, each with its own recorded ruling — #661 ("never
#                        present in GH (operator out-of-band), so registry
#                        content confidentiality does not inherit the GH trust
#                        boundary"), #13209 (the hosted read-mode is an
#                        operator lever that no deploy may set), and #12894 (the
#                        record allocator's cutover lever, which is rolled per box
#                        only AFTER every graph is seeded and armed — a moment no
#                        deploy can know). Adopting the gate's default for any of
#                        them would reverse that decision; the route is to reopen
#                        THAT issue, not to drop the token.
#
# ROTATION: for a `gh-secret:` name, rotating the GitHub secret is the only step —
# the next deploy propagates it.
#
# ── ENTRY-POINT FOR A REVIEWER: every other name below names a managing source;
#    the recorded debt is closed (#4471). THREE names are NOT managed from version
#    control, all declared `fly-only:` at the bottom — `REGISTRY_STREAM_KEY`
#    (#661, reopenable), `TORTOISE_RECORD_SERVE` (#13209, a live operator
#    lever) and `TORTOISE_RECORD_ALLOCATE` (#12894, the allocator cutover lever).
#    Read ALL THREE blocks and each issue's `OVERRIDES:` marker before touching
#    any of them, and treat a new `fly-only:` entry as needing an owner
#    decision, not a convenience spelling.
#
# ⛔ THE OTHER HALF OF THE CONTRACT — A DECLARED ABSENCE: this file says what the
#    deploy MANAGES. `.github/scripts/fly-secret-mitigations.txt` (#11122) says
#    what it must NOT manage for now, on purpose: a secret an operator removed as
#    the LIVE mitigation for an incident. A name in that ledger is still declared
#    `gh-secret:` HERE (the GitHub secret remains its managing source) but the
#    sync step drops it from the payload, so the deploy neither re-stages nor
#    rotates it. Two deploys re-armed #11092's `SENTRY_DSN` mitigation on builds
#    that did not contain the fix, which is the defect that ledger closes. Read
#    ITS header before adding an entry; a `gh-secret:` line here is never on its
#    own an assertion that the name must exist on Fly.

# ── Managed from GitHub Actions secrets (deploy-hosted.yml) ───────────────────
FASTAPI_INTERNAL_KEY            gh-secret:FASTAPI_INTERNAL_KEY

# #4126: a deliberate flash-class override for session-capture extraction. The
# value is a model id, not a credential, so it is recorded in the deploy
# definition itself (`.github/workflows/deploy-hosted.yml`) and assigned
# UNCONDITIONALLY there — a GitHub secret may still override it. That is the fix
# for the #4126 half where "the GitHub secret is absent" and "deliberately using
# the default" were indistinguishable: the default is now explicit and versioned
# (`openrouter:google/gemini-2.5-flash`), and the deploy overwrites whichever
# value was hand-set on Fly.
TORTOISE_SESSION_LLM_MODEL      workflow

# ── Assigned by the workflow, not currently present on Fly ────────────────────
# The deploy sets each of these on Fly once its GitHub secret exists (an
# alternate LLM provider, the #2318 backup-key rotation window, a custom
# transactional sender, Turnstile). They are declared so the gate cannot
# hard-fail the NEXT deploy after someone first sets one: the run that sets it
# passes (the guard runs before the propagation step) and every run after would
# report an undeclared Fly name. Declaring them is the reverse half of the
# contract — a Fly variable the workflow can assign must have a declaration.
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL              gh-secret:RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
BILLING_FROM_EMAIL              gh-secret:BILLING_FROM_EMAIL

# probe and its flyctl argv all carry VENICE_API_KEY once ingest._PROVIDERS
# registers the provider (hosted_api._LLM_PROVIDER_KEYS derives from it), so the
# assignment below has a declared managing source. Without this line the gate
# reports UNDECLARED — "assigned by deploy-hosted.yml but declared nowhere".
VENICE_API_KEY                  gh-secret:VENICE_API_KEY

# ── Set by the workflow from non-secret context ───────────────────────────────
TORTOISE_GIT_SHA                workflow   # ${GITHUB_SHA}; recorded per deploy
TORTOISE_GIT_DIRTY              workflow   # #10447: `git status --porcelain` at deploy time — was the BUILT tree the commit the sha names? `false` is a positive claim, so it is only staged when the tree is provably clean
BACKUP_SWEEP_ENABLED            workflow   # composed from the backup/R2/DR secret set

# ── TORTOISE_CAPTURE_IN_FLIGHT — a numeric TUNABLE, not a secret ───────────────
# The hosted capture lane's in-flight ceiling. Assigned UNCONDITIONALLY by the
# deploy from the versioned default in `.github/workflows/deploy-hosted.yml`
# (`ARGS+=(TORTOISE_CAPTURE_IN_FLIGHT=16)`, in the workflow-context group after
# `TORTOISE_GIT_DIRTY`) — that line IS the managing source: it is in version
# control, visible in CI, rotates with a PR, and overwrites whatever value is
# hand-set on Fly with the same number on the next deploy.
#
# WHY IT IS DECLARED AT ALL — the 2026-11-21 → 11-23 deploy outage. An operator
# hand-set it on `tortoise-y4mjjq` during the #12992 429 investigation (raising
# the ceiling past the code default of 8) with NO managing source, so the
# fail-closed provenance gate refused every `deploy-hosted` run in that window
# with:
#   UNDECLARED — 'TORTOISE_CAPTURE_IN_FLIGHT' is on Fly but declared nowhere in
#   fly-managed-secrets.txt
# and nothing merged in those two days was live. That is exactly the #4126
# defect class this registry exists to catch, and the gate was RIGHT to be red:
# the state was the defect, not the gate.
#
# ⛔ OVERRIDES: this repo's route for a NON-SECRET config value is `fly-toml-env`
#    (`fly.toml [env]` — the route every other #4126 config name takes, and the
#    route #13923 used for `TORTOISE_EMBEDDER_WARMUP`) — refused HERE because
#    that route cannot be COMPLETED from a lane. Route (b) requires
#    `flyctl secrets unset <NAME>` on a box that has `flyctl` and a Fly token,
#    and while the Fly secret still exists the `fly-toml-env` arm is RED BY
#    DESIGN (“declared fly-toml-env but is also a Fly secret”), so a `fly-toml-env`
#    declaration merged from a box with no Fly token would leave the gate red
#    and the deploy blocked, with no lane able to clear it. The `workflow` route
#    needs no unset and no bypass: the deploy ASSIGNS the name, so the value is
#    stated in version control AND the hand-set Fly value is overwritten with it.
#    (Recorded as a deliberate departure, not an oversight. The `fly-toml-env`
#    end state is strictly better hygiene — it would let
#    `check-fly-machine-env.py` assert the RUNNING machine carries the value
#    (#4568) and would make a future hand-set secret fail the gate; the exact
#    migration is the #4126 route (b) block above, for an operator holding the
#    token.)
#
# THE VALUE IS `16` BECAUSE THAT IS THE LIVE SETTING CARRIED ACROSS — not the
# code default `8`. A deploy that silently reverted it to 8 would re-open the
# 429 that parked 500+ sessions (#12992: a 724 → 908 entry backlog inside one
# session), so preserving it is part of
# the declaration, not a policy choice. `16` is also the ceiling
# `hosted_api._CAPTURE_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` clamps to (`max(1, min(env, 16))`), so this
# entry cannot exceed it. Carrying the value across settles nothing about the
# ceiling's policy: raising the in-flight ceiling is explicitly NOT #12992's fix
# (epic #14342), the hosted capture cap is HELD (#10175), and no product cap
# moves here (#4010).
TORTOISE_CAPTURE_IN_FLIGHT      workflow

# ── Adopted from the Fly-only hand-set set under #4126 ────────────────────────
# Both already exist as GitHub Actions secrets, so declaring them here makes the
# deploy the managing source: the value on Fly stops being hand-set, and a
# rotation from GitHub is the only step needed for it to take effect.
# NOTE: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ← SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY — the GitHub secret has
# the legacy name; the Fly variable keeps the RuntimeEnv name the app reads
# (tools/capture_cost_report.py accepts either, tortoise/ reads the *_ROLE_* one).
SUPABASE_URL                    gh-secret:SUPABASE_URL
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY       gh-secret:SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY

# ── Resolved under #4126 — the seven recorded-debt names ─────────────────────
# #4126's acceptance was that the deploy gate FAILS on this state, so the gate
# was correct to be red; it is the STATE that is fixed, not the gate. Six of the
# seven were convergent fixes (there was no decision to make): a non-secret
# config value belongs in version-controlled env, a secret belongs in CI
# secrets. The seventh is a recorded decision and gets its own category.
#
# CONFIG (non-secret) — route (b): the value's home is `fly.toml [env]` (the
# deploy applies it — versioned — and no Fly secret then needs to exist), and the
# Fly secret of the same name is UNSET
# (`flyctl secrets unset <NAME> --app tortoise-y4mjjq`).
#
# ⛔ WRITE PRODUCTION'S CURRENT VALUE, NEVER `.env.example`'s DEFAULT. The `[env]`
# value becomes effective the moment the secret is unset — until then the secret
# SHADOWS it and nothing you deploy for it is observable — so the value written
# here is the value production then runs. Confirm the live effective value first
# (#4471's caution for whoever executes this route). The `.env.example` vs live
# `0`/`1` divergence on `TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED` is the general case,
# not a one-off.
#
# ⛔ `fly.toml` IS THE ONLY DURABLE HOME. The deploy re-materialises the machine's
# env from `fly.toml`, so any `[env]` value that is not in the MERGED `fly.toml`
# is removed by the next `deploy-hosted` run — with no gate, warning or test to
# say so (#4568). Never set the value out-of-band (`secrets set` / `machine
# update`), and never deploy a PRE-merge `fly.toml`: step 1 below is merged first.
#
# ⛔ ORDER MATTERS — THE `[env]` VALUE MUST BE ON THE MACHINE BEFORE THE UNSET.
# While the secret exists THIS gate fails the name — `declared fly-toml-env but is
# also a Fly secret` — exit 1, before `flyctl deploy` runs, so a push-triggered
# deploy is RED on this name and cannot apply `[env]` unless a bypass is armed —
# and the only lane a push run has is the PERSISTENT repo variable, which this
# transition must not use (it would stay set). No other declaration survives that
# either (`unmanaged` → UNSOURCED; no entry → UNDECLARED; `fly-only:#N` →
# rejected for an `[env]` key; `gh-secret:` → needs a GitHub secret that does not
# exist for a value living only on Fly, and creating one is route (a), not route
# (b)). So:
#   1. land the `[env]` entry at production's CURRENT value (see the ⛔ above)
#      + this declaration, merged;
#   2. apply `[env]` with a `deploy-hosted` dispatch OF THE MERGED COMMIT
#      carrying the PER-RUN input `skip-fly-secret-provenance: true` (an
#      exit-1-class bypass, reported in the run summary). Use the dispatch INPUT,
#      never the repo variable — the input is consumed by the run, so nothing is
#      left set. CONFIRM THIS NAME'S SHADOW IS THE ONLY VIOLATION: the bypass
#      releases EVERY exit-1 violation in the run, and the summary names the
#      gate, not the violations (they are in the step log). The secret still
#      shadows `[env]`, so the value the app reads does not change. (A config-
#      only operator deploy of the current image — how #4523 did it — also
#      applies `[env]`, but runs none of the deploy gates and leaves no run
#      summary or audit line: this dispatch is the route.)
#   3. WAIT FOR THE DEPLOY JOB, NOT THE RUN — a `deploy-hosted` RUN can end RED
#      with `[env]` already applied: since #4538 the separate, fail-closed
#      `post-deploy-verify` job fails AFTER `flyctl deploy` succeeded. (Since
#      #10155 that workflow's `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` is FALSE, so a
#      later merge no longer cancels a RUNNING deploy after its Deploy step —
#      the `[env]`-applied / RUN-RED shape is now `post-deploy-verify` failing,
#      not a cancellation.)
#      So require the `deploy-api` job's Deploy step to succeed — unsetting
#      against a deploy that did NOT apply `[env]` drops the value. Only then:
#      `flyctl secrets unset <NAME> --app tortoise-y4mjjq`;
#   4. verify BOTH: `flyctl secrets list -a tortoise-y4mjjq` must no longer list
#      `<NAME>` (the shadow is gone — this list is the gate's own input), AND
#      `printenv <NAME>` on the machine must still return the value from step 1
#      (the move is behaviour-preserving). Neither alone is enough: `secrets
#      list` says nothing about the value, and `printenv` alone cannot say WHICH
#      source supplied it.
#
# The order relies on Fly applying `[env]` at deploy and preserving the machine
# config across a `secrets unset`; nothing asserts the running env (that is
# #4568's other half), so step 4 is the only check on the outcome — run both
# halves. A push-triggered deploy between (1) and (3) is red on this name BY
# DESIGN (the transitional state is the one the gate cannot express), so finish
# (3) as soon as step 2's Deploy step succeeds — and do NOT clear that freeze with
# `vars.SKIP_FLY_SECRET_PROVENANCE`, which leaves the incident-class lane armed.
#
# ⛔ WHY THE MERGED COMMIT — the #4568 evidence. A PRE-merge `[env]` application
# was removed by the next `deploy-hosted` run re-applying `main`'s `fly.toml`
# (which lacked the entries), and the value stayed ABSENT for ~5 h
# (TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED flipped off). Unset-first reaches that same
# absent state directly, with no revert needed.
#
# `TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED` moved as the LIVE value (`1`), not
# `.env.example`'s documented dev default (`0`) — the move is
# behaviour-preserving and the flag's value remains the owner's call.
TORTOISE_CONTROL_PLANE          fly-toml-env
TORTOISE_REAUTH_WINDOW_SECONDS  fly-toml-env
TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED fly-toml-env

# TORTOISE_EMBEDDER_WARMUP — route (b) of the #4126 block: a non-secret FLAG
# whose home is `fly.toml [env]`. It arrived as an UNDECLARED Fly secret —
# declared NOWHERE, which is the gate's UNDECLARED state and what failed every
# deploy since at least 2026-11-19T19:47Z — NOT as one of #4126's recorded-debt
# names; see #13923.
#
# The `[env]` value was carried across as the value MEASURED at the move (`0`),
# not as a standing fact. ⛔ While a Fly secret of this name is live IT supplies
# the value and `[env]` is SHADOWED, so `0` is what step 4 of the block above has
# to find still in force — re-measure it there rather than quoting this line
# (`fly.toml` states the same thing about the same value). The VALUE is the
# owner's call and this entry does not settle it (fly.toml records the same
# caution). ONE declaration gates the whole WARM-UP surface —
# `entrypoint.sh::_prewarm_embedder`, `EmbeddingModel.start_warm_up` (+ `warm_up`)
# at SDK engine init, and the hosted lifespan pre-warm, whose earlier
# flag-blindness is #7809 — so a flip arms all three. The switch does NOT gate
# `EmbeddingModel.get()` on the REQUEST path, but `0` also selects the
# request-path BOUNDS (`await_write_ready_reason` / `await_read_ready_reason`
# return None at `0`: #13224 / #13528), so a cold READ — or a `bounded=True`
# write fold — blocks the whole load instead of taking its own leg's degradation:
# a keyword-only read, or a row written WITHOUT a vector. (An UNBOUNDED
# record-truth write blocks at either value by design, #5004: the flag moves
# only the reads and the bounded folds.)
#
# A Fly secret of this name SHADOWS `[env]`, and this `fly-toml-env` arm refuses
# that state, so the gate is red on this name until the shadow is unset. The
# window and its order are NOT restated here — they are the #4126 route (b)
# block above, which owns the steps and their failure modes; follow that block.
# Tracked in #13923.
TORTOISE_EMBEDDER_WARMUP        fly-toml-env
# #10093: the per-graph ACL layer's DECLARED posture (#8617). NON-SECRET config
# versioned in `fly.toml [env]`, so it takes the `fly-toml-env` route — the same
# route as the four siblings above, and NOT in tension with it. Declaring it is
# what makes the shadow rejectable: the `fly-toml-env` arm FAILS on a Fly secret
# of this name (a secret would shadow the versioned value), so "not a secret"
# and "declared here" are one position, not opposite ones. What it must never
# acquire is a Fly SECRET of that name.
#
# Declared rather than left silent for one measured reason:
# `check-fly-machine-env.py` iterates ONLY the names the manifest declares
# `fly-toml-env` (its docstring: "For every name the manifest declares
# fly-toml-env"), and `deploy-hosted.yml` runs it AFTER the release precisely
# because a declared `[env]` value the RUNNING MACHINE does not carry passes
# every other gate there is (#4568: TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED was applied
# out of band, then reverted, and a product flag was off for ~5 h with nothing
# red). Undeclared, the DECLARED posture of the ACL layer is invisible to that
# gate: an out-of-band revert or a stale machine would silently fall back to
# `strict` in production with nothing turning red.
#
# ⚠️ What that costs is POSTURE, not availability — stated precisely, because the
# obvious reading is wrong. It does NOT re-introduce the #8617 outage: since
# `AclLayerDenied` was split from `AclLayerError`, a refusal is a `denied`
# RESULT and never a rollback, so a hosted mint succeeds under `strict` too (no
# 503). What is lost is the declaration itself: `off` answers
# `absent_by_design` BEFORE any server contact, so losing it silently turns every
# mint back into a per-mint `ACL` attempt that is refused and reported as
# `denied` — a per-graph round trip for a command this lane can never run, and
# a report that says "the credential was refused" where the truth is "this
# deployment declared the layer unavailable". Recorded, and gated, for that.
# (The manifest side would still catch a Fly *secret* of this name as a missing
# declaration; the MACHINE side is the half only this declaration reaches.)
TORTOISE_ACL_LAYER              fly-toml-env
# #8218: the consent screen's CLIENT-IDENTITY ALLOWLIST — non-secret, human-authored
# config, so it takes the same route as the five names above: versioned in
# `fly.toml [env]` (currently the documented default `"{}"` = attest nobody) and
# declared here. Declared rather than left silent for the same two reasons:
# (a) the `fly-toml-env` arm FAILS on a Fly SECRET of this name (a secret shadows
#     `[env]`, so the versioned value would not be what the app reads) — and a
#     hand-set secret is the #4126 defect, unsourced and unrotatable; and
# (b) `check-fly-machine-env.py` iterates ONLY the names declared `fly-toml-env`,
#     so undeclared this value could silently revert on a stale machine (#4568)
#     and the consent screen would quietly stop showing any attested client.
# ⛔ It must NEVER acquire a Fly secret of that name, and it does not live in
# `config/required-bindings.yml` — that manifest is the Cloudflare Pages surface,
# whose Functions do not import `tortoise/client_identity.py` (its only reader,
# in this Fly app). See `docs/oauth-mcp.md` §"Knobs".
TORTOISE_OAUTH_ATTESTED_CLIENTS fly-toml-env
# #2850 / #10585: the HARD loop-stall ceiling — non-secret, versioned config, so
# it takes the same route as the six names above. `fly.toml [env]` arms it at
# `600` while its SOFT sibling `TORTOISE_LOOP_STALL_EXIT_S` stays unset, and the
# deploy applies `[env]`, so no Fly secret needs to exist.
#
# Declared rather than left silent (#10585 review P2), for the same measured
# reason as its siblings: `check-fly-machine-env.py` — the post-deploy gate at
# `deploy-hosted.yml` — iterates ONLY the names this manifest declares
# `fly-toml-env`. Undeclared, the state "production was deployed and the RUNNING
# MACHINE does not carry the ceiling" passed every gate there is, and the only
# signal was `_loop_stall_hard_exit_s()` returning `0.0` INSIDE the process. That
# is the #4568 class, and here the thing silently lost is the wedge ceiling
# itself: a stale machine or a recreate that drops the `[env]` value disarms the
# self-heal with no gate, no warning and no red — the "silent hang" this knob
# exists to bound.
# ⛔ It must NEVER acquire a Fly secret of that name (a secret shadows `[env]`,
# so the versioned 600 would not be what the app reads) and the deploy must never
# stage it; the `fly-toml-env` arm fails on both.
TORTOISE_LOOP_STALL_HARD_EXIT_S fly-toml-env
# SECRETS — route (a): adopted by the deploy. The GitHub Actions secret was
# created from the LIVE Fly value (the value never entered a log or a
# transcript), the propagation line was added to deploy-hosted.yml, and the
# matching GH_SECRETS_PRESENT probe line was added with it (a `gh-secret:`
# declaration with no probe line reads as ABSENT and fails the deploy).
TORTOISE_AUDIT_DSN              gh-secret:TORTOISE_AUDIT_DSN   # Supabase pooler DSN (audit_events; #669/#771)
# NOT an adoption: this one is declared AHEAD of its value (#9548 / epic #7879
# R1). No such GitHub secret exists yet and no such Fly secret exists yet, so the
# guarded propagation is a no-op and the record stays NOT_ARMED — the state the
# epic's §A8 census measured, not a regression this declaration introduces. It is
# declared here so the name has a managing source THE MOMENT the operator creates
# the GitHub Actions secret: the next deploy stages it to Fly and the record turns
# on, with no second code change. The alternative — hand-setting it on Fly — is
# the #4126 defect (unsourced, unrotatable) and the gate correctly BLOCKS it.
TORTOISE_RECORD_DSN             gh-secret:TORTOISE_RECORD_DSN   # Postgres record arming DSN (epic #7879 R1, #9548)
TORTOISE_LINK_INTENT_SECRET     gh-secret:TORTOISE_LINK_INTENT_SECRET   # HMAC key for link-intent refs (#1765)
# #3524 §9 step 1 — the consent token's HMAC key (`tortoise/consent_token.py`).
# DEDICATED: §2.3 forbids reusing the service-role key or the anon key — the anon key is
# public BY CONSTRUCT (Supabase designs it to be "safe to expose online" and bounds it only
# by Row Level Security) and it sits in this API's own environment, so a collision with this
# key is OBSERVABLE. The verifier refuses a reused one with a typed 503 naming the collision.
# ⛔ "public by construct" is a property of the KEY, NOT a description of what this app sends
# to a browser: #4054 removed the dashboard's UMD bundle, #4178 keeps
# `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` non-load-bearing, and #3524 §9 step 4 deleted the consent page
# and its inline client. Do not read the sentence above as "we already publish it".
# ⛔ ROTATION IS `kid`-SCOPED SINCE #10794, NOT A VALUE SWAP. §2.1/§2.3 state a two-`kid`
# overlap window and that window is now BUILT (`CONSENT_TOKEN_KEYS` below): every kid in the set
# VERIFIES and only the current one MINTS, so publish-new / accept-both / retire-old no longer
# invalidates in-flight assertions for their <=120 s TTL. ⚠️ `kid` is LOAD-BEARING (the AS SELECTS
# the key by it), so a MIXED deployment is order-sensitive and the set must NAME the kid an
# un-migrated half stamps (`consent-1`) — the procedure, and why the key-drift fingerprint cannot
# see a `kid` split, are in docs/engineering/auth/consent-identity-bridge.md §2.3 / §2.5.
# It must be at least 32 UTF-8 BYTES; the API treats a shorter value as unprovisioned
# rather than signing with it, because a guessable HMAC key is the same forgery oracle.
CONSENT_TOKEN_SECRET            gh-secret:CONSENT_TOKEN_SECRET
# #10794: the `kid`-keyed key SET — the AS half of §2.3's rotation window. Declared so §2.3 step 1
# has an OPERABLE route: without this line the only way to set it on the AS was a hand-set
# `fly secrets set`, which the provenance gate below refuses as UNDECLARED — so the rotation the
# change advertises could not be delivered to the deployment it exists for (#13721 review, Issue 1).
# OPTIONAL by construction: guarded `gh-secret:`, so an absent GitHub secret stages nothing and the
# AS stays on the single-secret shape above, which is a fully supported deployment. The costs the
# guard implies are stated where the guard lives (`deploy-hosted.yml`, the probe + `ARGS+=` pair):
# while the GitHub secret is absent the name is CONDITIONALLY PROPAGATED, and if a Fly secret of
# this name is hand-set the gate reports UNSOURCED rather than letting the value sit unmanaged.
CONSENT_TOKEN_KEYS              gh-secret:CONSENT_TOKEN_KEYS
# `CONSENT_TOKEN_CURRENT_KID` — which kid MINTS. NOT a secret (it is a `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` name),
# so its home is `fly.toml [env]` => `fly-toml-env`, the route the other non-secret knobs take
# (`TORTOISE_OAUTH_ATTESTED_CLIENTS`, #8218). That route is what makes a Fly SECRET of this name
# fail the gate as a shadow, and it keeps a rotation's ordering in version control. The versioned
# value is `""` on purpose: absent/empty resolves to the FIRST kid in `CONSENT_TOKEN_KEYS`
# (declared order), so the ordinary rotation is ONE variable's value and needs no edit here.
CONSENT_TOKEN_CURRENT_KID       fly-toml-env
SENTRY_DSN                      gh-secret:SENTRY_DSN   # error tracking; activates only when set

# ── Decision-backed exception: deliberately Fly-only (NOT `unmanaged`) ───────
# #661 is a CLOSED recorded decision: this key must be "never present in GH
# (operator out-of-band), so registry content confidentiality does not inherit
# the GH trust boundary", with its own E2E — "a GH workflow cannot decrypt a
# registry archive with the Fly-only key". Its `OVERRIDES:` marker is on #661.
# Moving it into a GitHub secret would REVERSE that security decision; retiring
# it would break registry streaming. So it is neither — it is declared, and the
# issue carries the ruling. Rotation stays out-of-band:
#   tools/rotate-backup-keys.py --role registry_stream
REGISTRY_STREAM_KEY             fly-only:#661

# ── Decision-backed exception: a live out-of-band ARMED-MODE lever ───────────
# #13209 carries the ruling (its `OVERRIDES:` marker is on the issue): the
# hosted read-mode is an OPERATOR lever, not deploy-managed config. It is armed
# out-of-band with `flyctl secrets set TORTOISE_RECORD_SERVE=prefer` and
# reverted with `flyctl secrets unset` — docs/infra-runbook.md §"Arming the READ
# path — `TORTOISE_RECORD_SERVE` (epic #7879, #12941)" (the surface #13096 added
# for #13093), which states it verbatim: "Arming is an OWNER action. Nothing in
# the code arms it, and no deploy sets it."
#
# ⛔ NEITHER VERSION-CONTROL ROUTE FITS, AND BOTH WERE MEASURED (2026-11-17):
#   * `gh-secret:` makes the deploy the managing source, i.e. the deploy WOULD set
#     it — the ruling above, reversed. It is also unavailable TODAY: `gh api
#     repos/…/actions/secrets` returns 47 names and carries no
#     TORTOISE_RECORD_SERVE, so the declaration would fail this same gate as
#     ABSENT until an operator creates the GitHub secret AND its probe line.
#   * `fly-toml-env` would VERSION today's value into `fly.toml [env]` — again
#     the deploy setting it — and it breaks the published revert: with an `[env]`
#     value, `flyctl secrets unset` no longer returns the shipped default (`off`)
#     but the `[env]` value, so turning the mode off would need a code change
#     instead of the one operator step the runbook documents.
#   * `unmanaged` is the #4126 defect. Never an option.
# The absence of a version-control source IS the property here, which is exactly
# what this token records: deliberately unversioned, owner of the lever named,
# ruling checkable on the issue.
#
# ⚠️ TWO THINGS THIS LINE DOES NOT CLAIM. (1) It is NOT a credential — a
# three-mode read selector (`off` default / `prefer` / `record`) with no secret
# material, living in Fly's secret store only because that is the app's sole
# operator-settable channel. (2) It is a LIVE state, not a permanent one: the
# checker REFUSES a `fly-only:` name that no longer exists on Fly, so the
# documented `flyctl secrets unset` must delete this line in the same change.
# That is fail-closed and right — the exception is for a REAL out-of-band secret,
# so the revert is visible in review rather than silently stale.
TORTOISE_RECORD_SERVE           fly-only:#13209
# #12894: the allocator cutover ARMS the box AFTER every graph is seeded and armed
# (`tools/record_allocator_cli.py`'s `CUTOVER_ACK_TEXT` is the authority for that
# order). Default OFF. It is an operator lever rolled on purpose, per box, at a
# moment no deploy can know — an assignment from CI would either arm an unseeded
# graph or never run at all, and the latter is the #4126 shape this file exists to
# make impossible. Declared `fly-only:` so the value is deliberate rather than
# undeclared; the checker REFUSES this line once the secret is unset, so dropping
# the lever is a visible one-line revert.
#
# ⚠️ UNSETTING IS NOT THE REVERT. On a graph that has been cut over the enumerated
# arm is refused on the CURSOR ROW, so clearing the flag turns the record path OFF
# rather than back to enumeration — the way back is `halt` -> `seed --journal` ->
# `reopen` -> `arm`. The operator procedure, the preconditions `arm` refuses
# without `--acknowledge-cutover`, and the note that `set`/`unset` restart the
# Machine are in docs/infra-runbook.md §"Arming the allocator's cutover —
# `TORTOISE_RECORD_ALLOCATE` (#12894)".
TORTOISE_RECORD_ALLOCATE        fly-only:#12894
